**BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN)** — At least 59 people lost their lives and more than 200 others sustained injuries early Thursday when a fire erupted at an upscale Bangkok nightclub, where approximately 1,000 revelers had gathered to celebrate the new year, according to Thai police.

Rescue officials surveyed the scene at the nightclub, where most victims perished from smoke inhalation or were trampled amid a chaotic rush to escape. Police have identified 30 of the deceased—29 Thai nationals and one Singaporean citizen.

The blaze broke out at the Santika nightclub at approximately 12:35 a.m., authorities reported. Rescue teams confirmed that 226 people were injured, among them several foreign nationals. A U.S. State Department official confirmed that two Americans were injured in the fire, though the official withheld their names and the severity of their injuries, noting only that the department remained in contact with them.

Steven Hall, a British national injured in the fire, recounted to CNN how flames began spreading across the ceiling above the stage where a band and DJ were performing. Remarkably, some attendees initially mistook the fire for part of the show.

"At the same time there were people rushing to get out, there were other people who seemed to be lacking a sense of urgency and didn't seem to realize what was going on," Hall explained.

According to police Major General Chokchai Deeprasertwit, the fire originated near the stage, where fireworks had been incorporated into the performance marking the club's final night of operation.

"He immediately ran out of the building, but immediately when he'd done that, the lights went out, and he couldn't see," Jones recounted.

Dr. Anong Preechapanich, director of emergency services at a nearby hospital, said many victims suffered severe burns and smoke inhalation. "We are dealing with a mass casualty event unlike anything we've seen in this district. Several patients remain in critical condition, and we expect the death toll may still rise," she said during a press briefing Wednesday morning.

As of the latest update from Thailand's Ministry of Public Health, 47 people are confirmed dead, though officials cautioned that number could climb as search teams comb through the charred structure and hospitals continue treating the injured. At least 15 patients remain in intensive care.

## Venue's Background Under Scrutiny

Mountain B nightclub had operated for several years as a nightlife destination known for large-scale events, drawing both local patrons and tourists during major holidays. Local media reports indicate the venue had previously faced complaints over crowd capacity and emergency exit accessibility, though it is unclear whether any formal violations had been issued prior to the fire.

Bangkok's governor, Chadchart Sittipunt, announced that a full investigation into the club's safety certifications, fire suppression systems, and structural compliance would be launched immediately. "Every nightclub and entertainment venue in this city will be inspected in the coming days," Chadchart said. "We owe it to the victims and their families to understand how this was allowed to happen."

Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin extended condolences to victims' families and ordered a nationwide review of nightlife venue safety standards, citing similar tragedies in the region in recent years.

## A Nation in Mourning

As news of the disaster spread, Thai citizens began holding vigils outside hospitals and at the site of the fire, lighting candles among charred debris. Flowers and photographs of the missing lined the street outside the club's blackened facade by Wednesday afternoon.

For survivors like Suthep, the physical scars may heal faster than the emotional ones. "I keep thinking about the people I couldn't help," he said. "We came to celebrate a new beginning. Instead, so many people lost everything."

Authorities say identification of victims is ongoing, with DNA testing required in several cases due to the severity of injuries. A hotline has been established for families searching for missing loved ones.
